items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The guards are short and explain themselves, and each has a comment saying why: `if self.field.is_cached(rel_obj): continue  # Don't override a value set by a nested prefetch.` The formatting matches the surrounding code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Uses the existing is_cached API and adds no new bookkeeping. The same three-line guard appears in three sibling methods. Each of those methods already had its own loop, so this follows the existing structure rather than copy-pasting logic. No dead code; the throwaway tests were deleted.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed, no magic constants are added, and the guards are conditional. When nothing is cached, the original code path still runs. All 388 related tests pass, as do the hidden tests (P2P 85/85).

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: The reverse-FK manager is guarded with `self.field.is_cached(rel_obj)`. ReverseOneToOneDescriptor uses the same guard (`self.related.field.is_cached`), and so does ForwardManyToOneDescriptor (`remote_field.is_cached`). When the relation isn't cached, the reverse link is still set. The agent tested both the one-to-one and the FK case.
